questions.question: What distinguishes a ring from an abelian group?
options: A ring has a second operation that is associative and distributes over addition
A ring requires every element to have a multiplicative inverse
A ring forbids commutativity of addition
A ring is always finite
questions.explanation: A ring is an abelian group under addition with an additional associative multiplication that distributes over addition. Multiplicative inverses are not required.

questions.question: Which subset of Z/12Z is NOT an ideal?
questions.explanation: {0, 1} fails additive closure (1 + 1 = 2) and absorption (2 * 1 = 2). The other three are principal ideals (6), (3), and (4).

questions.question: What does the absorption rule require of an ideal I in a ring R?
options: For every r in R and s in I, both r * s and s * r lie in I
Every element of R must equal some element of I
The product of any two elements of I must equal 1
I must contain the multiplicative identity
questions.explanation: Absorption: multiplying any ring element by any ideal element stays in the ideal. This is precisely what makes coset multiplication well-defined.

questions.question: Why is Z/nZ a field exactly when n is prime?
options: When n is prime, every nonzero element is coprime to n, so it has a multiplicative inverse
Composite n always lacks an additive identity
Prime n forces multiplication to be non-commutative
Prime n removes the need for distributivity
questions.explanation: For prime n, gcd(a, n) = 1 for every nonzero a, so every nonzero element is a unit. Composite n produces zero divisors and breaks invertibility.

questions.question: In Z/12Z, what is the principal ideal (4)?
options: All multiples of 4 in Z

questions.question: How many cosets does Z/12Z / (3) have?
questions.explanation: The ideal (3) = {0, 3, 6, 9} has 4 elements; |Z/12Z| / |(3)| = 12 / 4 = 3 cosets, with canonical representatives 0, 1, 2.

questions.question: Why must I be an ideal — not just an additive subgroup — for R/I to be a ring?
options: Without absorption, multiplication of cosets depends on the representative chosen
Without absorption, addition of cosets becomes non-associative
Without absorption, the zero coset disappears
Without absorption, the cosets cease to partition R
questions.explanation: Coset multiplication (a + I)(b + I) = ab + I is well-defined only because r * s lands in I for every r in R and s in I.

questions.question: Which cryptographic object is the quotient ring F_2[x] / (x^8 + x^4 + x^3 + x + 1)?
options: The AES finite field GF(2^8)
The RSA group (Z/nZ)*
The secp256k1 scalar field
The Kyber polynomial ring
questions.explanation: AES arithmetic happens in GF(2^8), constructed as the quotient of F_2[x] by the irreducible polynomial x^8 + x^4 + x^3 + x + 1.
